name: Fornfrusenen

related.relation: older than her citadel; the giants cut around him

facts.text: Fornfrusenen is a level-75 being with 100,000 health that wakes from the ice walls; he takes no damage from attackers further than 200 from him.
He hisses that he knows the name of the one who woke him, and that they will be entombed in the ice for eternity.
He raises two or three Fornfrusenen Shards, which only take damage from close range too; when he dies the shards evaporate.
The Midgard epic raid wiped at Fornfrusenen in the 2026-11-04 overnight runs: casters and archers do nothing to him.
Swedish forn means ancient and frusen frozen: roughly 'the long-frozen one' (to verify).
Bot chat guesses something has been frozen in that glacier since before the queen came.

story:
Fornfrusenen is older than the citadel. When Kula's giants cut their first tunnels through the north side of the glacier they found him already in the wall, a long shape asleep in clear ice, with a face that was not a giant's face and not a dragon's and not a man's. The tunnel-cutters would not work near him. They told the overseer something in the ice was watching them, and he laughed, and the next morning he did not laugh. So they cut around him instead, a great hollow in the ice, and left him there, because even hrimthursa have sense. The children of the glacier are told that if they shout in that hall the sleeper will learn their names. They do not shout there.

His name only means the long-frozen one. He does not mind; he has forgotten his own. He has not forgotten anyone else's. He knows the names of everyone who has walked past his wall in all the centuries he has been asleep, and when he is woken he knows yours. He tells you so, with a hiss and a laugh, as he steps out of the ice: look around you, he says, because this is where you will be entombed for all eternity. The old icesplitter who told me about him said he was older than the dragon under the citadel. Then he said he had said too much.

He cannot be hurt from a distance. The cold around him is so old and so deep that it swallows arrows and spells alike before they reach him; only a blade close enough to feel his breath will bite. The shards he raises from the walls are pieces of the same cold, two or three at a time, and they are the same: stand close, or do nothing. The frost of the shards shocks whoever is near them. Midgard's raids die here more than anywhere else in the glacier, the casters standing helpless at the back while the warriors try to do the work of a whole raid.

When he dies, the frosty glow in his eyes blinks out, and his shape fades slowly into the ice, and the shards evaporate as if they had never been. The hrimthursa hope that the promise goes with them. They are not sure. The wall is empty after, they say, but it is not smooth. It still has the shape of him.
legend: Fornfrusenen is a melee fight, full stop. Nothing hurts him from more than a couple of steps away: casters and archers do nothing past 200. Bring every tank and every melee you have, heal them hard, and kill the shards up close too. Casters buff, heal and rez. Don't drag him out of his hollow or he resets, and keep the fight going. More Midgard raids die here than anywhere else in the glacier; the Living Server's own raid wiped here. Nickname: the wall. Never shout in his hall, the old hands say. He learns your name. His shards evaporate when he dies, so don't waste time on the last ones.

aggro: I know your name. Look around you. This is where you will lie, forever.
Look around you. Within this ice you will lie forever.
Ahh. So many names. I will keep them all.

loremasterTopic.text: The long-frozen one. He was in the wall before the citadel was cut. He knows the name of whoever wakes him, and only a blade close enough to feel his breath will bite him.

bookPage: The tunnel-cutters would not work the north wall. They told the overseer something in it watched them, and he laughed, and the next morning he did not laugh. They cut around it instead, a great hollow in the ice, and left it sleeping. Hrimthursa children are told that if they shout in that hall it will learn their names. Hrimthursa children do not shout there. I asked one of the old icesplitters what it was. He said it was older than the dragon. Then he said he had said too much, and would not speak to me again, and the next time I came to Dellinstad he had gone back up to the glacier.
